title: KV cache sync-window race detection and longtail throttle playbook
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Follow-up to a capacity/regression incident where a race between async prefix index updates and slab compaction caused index desynchronization, leading to longtail eviction storms and tenant request latency spikes. This ticket tracks detection instrumentation, immediate mitigations, and code changes to remove the race and prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: On 2026-02-25 03:40 UTC we observed sustained 5-15x memory growth on a subset of kvcache shards serving LLM inference. Symptoms: increased OOM kill rate, request timeouts, and failover to fallback model variants. Root cause traced to a narrow timing window where concurrent compaction and prefix-index writeback produced stale index entries (index drift), which caused the eviction priority queue to ignore recently-accessed entries and trigger aggressive eviction of hot prefixes.
timeline: 2026-02-25 03:38 UTC - anomaly detected by heap-growth alert (shard_kvcache_heap > 70% for 5m)
2026-02-25 03:45 UTC - oncall paged; initial remediation toggled eviction_throttle=on cluster-wide
2026-02-25 04:10 UTC - temporary mitigation applied: reduce compaction concurrency from 8 -> 2
2026-02-25 05:00 UTC - memory growth stabilized but latency remained elevated
2026-02-26 10:00 UTC - deep-dive started; reproducer developed in stress lab with synthetic write patterns
2026-02-27 16:00 UTC - root-cause hypothesis validated: prefix-index writeback can write tombstones out-of-order under concurrent compact
2026-02-28 09:00 UTC - interim guardrails merged (PR #11234) to add index-checksum verification on compaction completion
2026-03-01 14:00 UTC - incident postmortem published (Confluence) and this follow-up ticket opened
root_cause: A race between async prefix-index writeback and slab compaction that allowed stale tombstone pointers to remain visible to the eviction heap. The eviction priority computation used a stale last-access timestamp due to non-atomic pointer swaps, causing eviction of hot prefixes and preventing KV reuse, cascading into memory amplification and request timeouts.
action_items: Short-term: add a per-shard compaction_inflight gauge and increase alert sensitivity (ops runbook) - OWNER: Marcus Lee - ETA: 2026-03-05
Short-term: deploy eviction throttles and backpressure that cap eviction rate per-tenant during high memory growth - OWNER: SRE Team - ETA: 2026-03-07

Short-term: enable index-checksum verification on compaction completion and auto-sweep mismatches to tombstone log - OWNER: Aisha Raman - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kvcache/pull/11234 - ETA: 2026-03-01 (deployed)

Medium-term: refactor prefix-index writeback to use atomic epoch fencing (epoch++ then write then commit marker) to prevent stale reads - OWNER: Marcus Lee - estimate 5 points - target release runtime-1.23
Medium-term: implement per-key linearizable updates for prefix metadata or adopt compare-and-swap for pointer swaps - OWNER: Storage Eng - estimate 8 points
Medium-term: add a telemetry pipeline that emits per-tenant evict_rate, stale_index_count, and compaction_conflicts with 1m granularity - OWNER: Observability - ETA: 2026-03-20
Long-term: build a chaos test harness exercising concurrent compaction/writeback/eviction under production-like load and add to pre-merge CI - OWNER: Reliability - estimate 13 points - ETA: 2026-Q2
Long-term: run tenant-level retention analysis and introduce fair-share eviction scoring to avoid tenant starvation during recovery - OWNER: Product & Storage Eng - ETA: 2026-Q3
acceptance_criteria: Index desync no longer reproducible in stress lab with previous repro workload
Per-shard compaction_inflight and stale_index_count metrics are visible in Grafana and alert when >0 for 2m
Eviction throttle prevents >2x baseline eviction rate for any tenant during memory spikes
Code change for atomic writeback merged and rolled out to canary cluster without regressions
Chaos test reproducer added and passing in CI for 4 consecutive runs
risks: Refactor for atomic writeback could induce temporary increased latency during write paths
Eviction throttle may increase memory retention in some edge cases; need careful canarying
Telemetry volume increase may require retention or indexing changes in Observability pipeline
runbook_updates: Add step: if shard_kvcache_heap > 80% for 3m, enable eviction_throttle and reduce compaction concurrency to 1
Add step: if stale_index_count > 10 for 5m, trigger emergency index-sweep job and page Storage Eng
notes: Oncall mitigations successfully prevented customer-visible data loss but highlighted gaps in telemetry for compaction conflicts
Customer impact concentrated on a small set of mid-market tenants with heavy prefix churn; engaged CSMs and issued incident notes
Observed unusual correlation with GC pauses on compactor workers; follow-up to add GC tuning to compactor config
